justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture satisfies all requirements: Fraud Scoring Engine handles real-time scoring (R-01), Case Management Backend and Analyst UI deliver case review workflows (R-02), and Model & Rule Registry Service with Model Hot-Swapper enables zero-downtime rule updates (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Sub-50ms P99 at 3,000 TPS is well supported by Go-based Fraud Scoring Engine, in-memory feature queries via Redis Cluster / Amazon ElastiCache, and offloading audit writes asynchronously through Amazon SQS / SNS to Asynchronous Audit Worker.
justifications.compatibility: Standard protocols ensure seamless integration: Payment Gateway connects via gRPC/HTTPS through API Gateway / Envoy, Fraud Analysts authenticate with external IdP / AWS Cognito via OIDC, and compliance exports integrate cleanly with AWS S3 Object Lock.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts are well accommodated by a dedicated Analyst UI delivered via CloudFront and S3, supported by Case Controller and dynamic masking via Masking & Authorization Interceptor to hide full card data.
justifications.reliability: Availability targets are met via API Gateway / Envoy's Circuit Breaker supporting fail-open operation to avoid blocking payments beyond 1 minute, Redis Sentinel failover, Aurora read replicas, and DLQ Handler for failed audit messages.
justifications.security: PCI-DSS and 7-year auditability are thoroughly addressed by Tokenization Filter, Masking & Authorization Interceptor, AWS Secrets Manager with automatic credential rotation, TLS 1.3, and write-once compliance logging to AWS S3 Object Lock.
justifications.maintainability: Clear container separation between Fraud Scoring Engine, Case Management Backend, and Model & Rule Registry Service minimizes coupling. The Model Hot-Swapper and transactional outbox patterns allow a three-engineer team to operate and deploy updates safely.
justifications.portability: Tailored to AWS eu-west-1 using ECS Fargate, Lambda, and Aurora. Deep integration with proprietary services like S3 Object Lock, Secrets Manager, and AWS Cognito limits multi-cloud portability, though containerized workloads remain adaptable.

PERF-01.justification: The Go-based scoring engine evaluates rules via embedded WebAssembly and in-memory Redis feature lookups. Decoupled asynchronous audit publishing over buffered channels ensures low latency well within 50 ms at 3,000 TPS.
sensitivity_points: Redis cluster network latency and in-memory feature retrieval speed
Go channel buffer capacity preventing backpressure on scoring evaluator
tradeoffs: In-memory evaluation prioritized over synchronous database writes

PERF-02.justification: Scoring and case review traffic are completely isolated. Fraud scoring runs against Redis and in-memory engines, while analyst workflows interact through Spring Boot against Aurora PostgreSQL with read replica routing.
sensitivity_points: Separation of in-memory scoring path from relational database queries
tradeoffs: Read replicas add minor replication lag for analysts to preserve performance

AVAIL-01.justification: Envoy provides circuit breaking with outlier detection and fail-open routing, avoiding payment blockage. However, auditing fallback decisions when the engine is unavailable relies on access logs rather than dedicated fallback audit emitters.
sensitivity_points: Envoy circuit breaker threshold tuning for rapid sub-minute failure recovery
tradeoffs: Allowing payments on fail-open risks fraud exposure to prevent checkout disruption

AVAIL-02.justification: Audit events are emitted via buffered Go channels to an Amazon SNS/SQS pipeline decoupled from the scoring path. SQS and DLQ mechanics preserve events during downstream Lambda or S3 Object Lock degradation.
sensitivity_points: SQS retention limits and buffer depths during extended S3 outages
tradeoffs: Asynchronous logging decouples latency from compliance storage availability

MOD-01.justification: The Model Hot-Swapper performs atomic pointer swaps in memory without process restart or downtime. Models are pre-validated, compiled, and tagged with version metadata stored with each decision.
sensitivity_points: Thread-safe atomic pointer swaps ensure consistent model execution per transaction
tradeoffs: Local memory caching of models vs memory overhead across scoring instances

MOD-02.justification: New rules and velocity checks are deployed through the Model & Rule Registry Service to Redis sliding window limiters and the scoring engine hot-swapper. Decisions explicitly capture evaluated rule tags.
sensitivity_points: Coordination latency between registry distribution and scoring engine polling
tradeoffs: Dynamic rule distribution complexity versus zero-downtime execution speed

SEC-01.justification: A Tokenization Filter and Masking & Authorization Interceptor enforce that plain PAN data is unreachable by analysts. Although access is logged via CloudTrail, automated alerting for anomalous analyst access within 15 minutes is not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: Consistent masking rules enforced in interceptors before sending data to Analyst UI
tradeoffs: Data masking protects cardholder data but limits analyst visibility during triage

SEC-02.justification: The Asynchronous Audit Worker formats and writes decision payloads, model versions, and hash chains to AWS S3 Object Lock configured for 7-year WORM retention, enabling reproducible audit reports within one business day.
sensitivity_points: Immutability policies on S3 Object Lock buckets and key retention duration
tradeoffs: Write-once storage cost versus long-term compliance audit reliability
